subject: Per-token anchoring and CPI safeguard discussion for Lumina
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <samuel.park@lumina.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumina.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Per-token anchoring and CPI safeguard discussion for Lumina

Samuel —

Thanks again for the time earlier. We ran numbers on the trial footprint you shared and wanted to propose an initial committed plan that balances predictable unit economics for you with our ability to honor performance and capacity guarantees: 

Proposed commercial anchor (starter):
- Commitment: $150,000/month (hosted API) for 12 months
- Discount: 20% off published per-token rates for committed usage; overage at retail per-token (no retroactive blending)
- Price lock: 12 months on per-token base price for the committed tiers

Open items we expect your procurement/legal to flag: MFN language (scope/carveouts), CPI indexing or annual price adjustments, and whether you need a strict price floor for renewals. Curious where Lumina sits on those items — are you expecting an MFN that covers private channel offers or public list prices only? And do you have a target cap for CPI adjustments?

I can loop in Marissa (pricing lead) and Neha (revenue ops) to surface sample contract language and an illustrative breakdown. Attached is a short summary of the commitment economics (will share a more formal MA plan if this looks directionally correct).

Attachment: Lumina_Redwood_MAPlan_v3.pdf (summary of tiers)

Next step: if the anchor looks reasonable, can we get procurement availability for a short call this week to align on MFN/CPI expectations and any required carveouts?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Per-token anchoring and CPI safeguard discussion for Lumina

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear proposal. A couple of quick clarifying questions from procurement/legal before we bring in commercial ops: 

1) MFN: Lumina typically requests MFN scoped to published public offers and partner portals — we generally exclude channel-only promotions. Would Redwood be willing to accept MFN limited to public list pricing?
2) CPI cap: ops wants a firm cap on annual price increases; would Redwood entertain a cap in the 3%–5% range?
3) Sample contract language: can you share the exact MFN and CPI wording you suggest so legal can redline?

Looping Alyssa (Lumina counsel) in case she wants to weigh in on language. We can do a short call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

—Samuel
Samuel Park
Head of Platform, Lumina AI
samuel.park@lumina.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <samuel.park@lumina.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Per-token anchoring and CPI safeguard discussion for Lumina

Samuel —

Quick note from pricing/ops on the two items you flagged. High level: we can meet Lumina halfway with protections that are operationally supportable for Redwood while giving you predictability. 

Proposed definitions / guardrails: 
- MFN: Redwood will provide a Most-Favored-Nation clause limited to publicly accessible list/pricing pages and partner portal published offers. MFN will explicitly exclude private channel partner discounts, beta/incentive pilots, and one-off strategic deals.

- Price lock & CPI cap: Redwood can lock the per-token base price for 12 months for the committed tier. For annual adjustments after the first year, we propose a CPI cap of 5% (annual) with a contractual floor of 0% (i.e., prices may not drop below the base committed price during the 12-month term). If Lumina increases committed volume by >=25% at renewal, we will apply a graduated discount step-down (improved unit price) instead of the CPI adjustment.

Operational notes: MFN checks will be scoped to public web listings and partner portal snapshots we maintain; we cannot reasonably monitor private partner negotiations. For CPI we will require a clause that references the U.S. CPI-U index and a 60‑day notice period for any indexed price change at renewal.

Attaching an annotated MA plan and a short sample MFN/CPI clause you can pass to Alyssa. Happy to hop on a call to walk through redline points.

Attachment: Lumina_Redwood_MAPlan_v3.pdf (annotated)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
marissa.c@redwood.com
From: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@luminalegal.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Park <samuel.park@lumina.ai>, procurement@lumina.ai
Date: 2026-12-10T15:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Per-token anchoring and CPI safeguard discussion for Lumina

Marissa / Vivek —

Thanks for the quick clarification. A few items legal will want tightened up in the commercial agreement draft: 

- MFN scope: we prefer MFN to public list prices plus reseller-public promotions (where the reseller publishes pricing). We will propose carveouts for confidential strategic agreements, but need the language to be explicit about what counts as a public offer.
- CPI cap: 5% is reasonable as a starting point; Lumina's finance team has pushed for a 3% cap. We are open to a compromise if Redwood can concede to 4.5% or provide an alternative such as a fixed percentage with a mid-term cap review tied to actual CPI movements.
- Remedy and audit: for MFN infractions we will want a short remedy window and a calculation approach (credit vs. rate adjustment).

I've drafted a few redline bullets and attached a doc with suggested language (redline-pricing-terms.docx). Can Marissa/Vivek confirm whether Redwood can do: (a) MFN to public + reseller-published offers; (b) CPI cap at 4.5%; and (c) a 90-day lookback/remedy window for MFN compliance credits?

Quoted for context: 
> On Thu, Dec 10, 2026 at 8:30 AM Marissa Cole wrote: 
> 
> > Proposed definitions / guardrails: 
> > - MFN: Redwood will provide a Most-Favored-Nation clause limited to publicly accessible list/pricing pages and partner portal published offers...
> > - Price lock & CPI cap: Redwood can lock the per-token base price for 12 months for the committed tier...

Attachment: redline-pricing-terms.docx (redline suggested language)

Best,
Alyssa Greene
Counsel, Lumina AI (external)
alyssa@luminalegal.com

Date: 2026-12-11T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Per-token anchoring and CPI safeguard discussion for Lumina

Samuel / Alyssa / team —

Appreciate the clarity. Summarizing the commercial position Redwood can take so everyone has a single source of truth before legal starts a formal redline: 

Agreed commercial points (proposed final):
- Commitment: $150k/month hosted API for 12 months (LUM-2026-0789)
- Discounts: 20% off published per-token rates for committed usage; overage billed at published retail per-token rates
- Price lock: 12 months on the per-token base price for the committed tier
- MFN: scope limited to (1) public list/pricing pages and (2) reseller-published, publicly visible promotions. Explicit carveouts: private strategic deals, invite-only pilots, and one-off channel incentive programs.
- CPI cap: Redwood will agree to a 4.5% annual cap on CPI-based increases after the initial 12-month lock (compromise from 5% to 4.5%). CPI reference: U.S. CPI-U; 60-day notice period at renewal.
- MFN remedy: if an MFN-triggering lower public price is found, Redwood will provide a credit for the differential for the prior 90 days (subject to proof and reasonable verification).

Next steps: 
1) Marissa/Neha and I will produce a short addendum reflecting the bullets above and submit to Alyssa for redline by end of day tomorrow.
2) Samuel/procurement to share PO template and preferred billing contact so finance can prepare SOW + invoice cadence.
3) I'll update the HubSpot deal (link below) and attach the MA plan and redline when ready.

Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/LUM-2026-0789

If that summary looks good, we should be able to move to signature and initial invoice within one week.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
